# receipts.sh — what the partner can actually download, per settlement day.
# Reads the partner's box through the transfer CLI and totals the detail rows.

# receipts_rows PARTNER — one line per header and per detail row of every file
# in the partner's box:
#   P<TAB>date<TAB>part<TAB>parts
#   D<TAB>date<TAB>net
receipts_rows() {
  local partner=$1 name bytes ticket
  xfer_ls "$partner" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r name bytes ticket; do
    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
    xfer_pull "$partner" "$name" | tr -d '\r' | awk -F, '
      $1 == "H" { split($5, pp, "/"); print "P\t" $4 "\t" pp[1] "\t" pp[2] }
      $1 == "D" { print "D\t" $3 "\t" $6 }'
  done
}

# receipts_day ROWS DATE -> "<count> <net>" for the day.
# A split day is totalled only once parts 1..n are all in the box; until then
# the answer is "0 0", the same as a day with no file at all.
# TODO: 일부 파트만 온 날도 온 만큼은 세어 주면 되지 않나? 지금은 '-'라 헷갈린다.
receipts_day() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk -F'\t' -v d="$2" '
    $1 == "P" && $2 == d { seen[$3 + 0] = 1; want = $4 + 0 }
    $1 == "D" && $2 == d { n++; s += $3 }
    END {
      have = 0
      for (p in seen) if (p >= 1 && p <= want) have++
      if (want == 0 || have < want) { print "0 0"; exit }
      print n + 0, s + 0
    }'
}

# receipts_report PARTNER FROM TO
receipts_report() {
  local partner=$1 from=$2 to=$3 rows d cnt net
  rows=$(receipts_rows "$partner")
  printf '# partner %s  %s..%s\n' "$partner" "$(date_dash "$from")" "$(date_dash "$to")"
  for d in $(date_range "$from" "$to"); do
    read -r cnt net <<< "$(receipts_day "$rows" "$d")"
    if [ "$cnt" -eq 0 ]; then
      printf '%s  %4s  %15s\n' "$(date_dash "$d")" "-" "-"
    else
      printf '%s  %4d  %15s\n' "$(date_dash "$d")" "$cnt" "$(money_fmt "$net")"
    fi
  done
}
----
# naming.sh — remote file names for settlement files.
#
#   HBP_SETTLE_<partner>_<YYYYMMDD>.csv          one file for the day
#   HBP_SETTLE_<partner>_<YYYYMMDD>-<n>.csv      day split into several parts
#
# The transfer service parks (never delivers) names with four or more '_',
# so the part number must not add another '_' field.

# settle_name PARTNER DATE PART PARTS
settle_name() {
  local partner=$1 date=$2 part=$3 parts=$4
  local base="${FILE_PREFIX}_${partner}_${date}"
  if [ "$parts" -gt 1 ]; then
    base="${base}-${part}"
  fi
  printf '%s.%s' "$base" "$FILE_EXT"
}
# manifest.sh — local record of what was handed to the transfer CLI.
# One line per file: date|partner|name|ticket|rows

manifest_file() { printf '%s/manifest.psv' "$OUT_DIR"; }

manifest_add() {
  ensure_dir "$OUT_DIR"
  printf '%s|%s|%s|%s|%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" >> "$(manifest_file)"
}

# A re-run of the same day appends new lines; keep only the latest line for
# each (date, partner, name).
manifest_compact() {
  local f tmp
  f=$(manifest_file)
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
  tmp="$f.tmp"

# receipts.sh — what the partner can actually download, per settlement day.
# Reads the partner's box through the transfer CLI and totals the detail rows.

# receipts_rows PARTNER — one line per header and per detail row of every file
# in the partner's box:
#   P<TAB>date<TAB>part<TAB>parts
#   D<TAB>date<TAB>net
receipts_rows() {
  local partner=$1 name bytes ticket
  xfer_ls "$partner" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r name bytes ticket; do
    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
    xfer_pull "$partner" "$name" | tr -d '\r' | awk -F, '
      $1 == "H" { split($5, pp, "/"); print "P\t" $4 "\t" pp[1] "\t" pp[2] }
      $1 == "D" { print "D\t" $3 "\t" $6 }'
  done
}

# receipts_day ROWS DATE -> "<count> <net>" for the day.
# A split day is totalled only once parts 1..n are all in the box; until then
# the answer is "0 0", the same as a day with no file at all.
# TODO: 일부 파트만 온 날도 온 만큼은 세어 주면 되지 않나? 지금은 '-'라 헷갈린다.
receipts_day() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk -F'\t' -v d="$2" '
    $1 == "P" && $2 == d { seen[$3 + 0] = 1; want = $4 + 0 }
    $1 == "D" && $2 == d { n++; s += $3 }
    END {
      have = 0
      for (p in seen) if (p >= 1 && p <= want) have++
      if (want == 0 || have < want) { print "0 0"; exit }
      print n + 0, s + 0
    }'
}

# receipts_report PARTNER FROM TO
receipts_report() {
  local partner=$1 from=$2 to=$3 rows d cnt net
  rows=$(receipts_rows "$partner")
  printf '# partner %s  %s..%s\n' "$partner" "$(date_dash "$from")" "$(date_dash "$to")"
  for d in $(date_range "$from" "$to"); do
    read -r cnt net <<< "$(receipts_day "$rows" "$d")"
    if [ "$cnt" -eq 0 ]; then
      printf '%s  %4s  %15s\n' "$(date_dash "$d")" "-" "-"
    else
      printf '%s  %4d  %15s\n' "$(date_dash "$d")" "$cnt" "$(money_fmt "$net")"
    fi
  done
}

# money.sh — integer KRW arithmetic and formatting.

# money_net AMOUNT FEE -> amount minus fee
money_net() { printf '%d' $(( 10#$1 - 10#$2 )); }

# money_fmt N -> "1,234,567"
money_fmt() {
  local n=$1 sign="" out=""
  case "$n" in -*) sign="-"; n=${n#-} ;; esac
  while [ ${#n} -gt 3 ]; do
    out=",${n: -3}$out"
    n=${n:0:${#n}-3}
  done
  printf '%s%s%s' "$sign" "$n" "$out"
}
# common.sh — logging, configuration loading and small guards shared by
# the wrapper and every step script.

log()  { printf '[%s] %s\n' "${PAYOUT_STEP:-payout}" "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf '[%s] warn: %s\n' "${PAYOUT_STEP:-payout}" "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf '[%s] error: %s\n' "${PAYOUT_STEP:-payout}" "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

load_conf() {
  local f="$PAYOUT_HOME/conf/payout.conf"
  [ -r "$f" ] || die "missing config $f"
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$f"
}

require_file() {
  [ -f "$1" ] || die "${2:-file} not found: $1"
  [ -r "$1" ] || die "${2:-file} not readable: $1"
}

ensure_dir() {
  mkdir -p "$1" 2>/dev/null || die "cannot create directory $1"
  [ -w "$1" ] || die "directory not writable: $1"
}

# Validates a business date in YYYYMMDD form and echoes it back.
check_date() {
  local d=$1
  case "$d" in
    [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;;
    *) die "bad date '$d' (want YYYYMMDD)" ;;
  esac
  local m=$((10#${d:4:2})) day=$((10#${d:6:2}))
  [ "$m" -ge 1 ] && [ "$m" -le 12 ] || die "bad month in $d"
  [ "$day" -ge 1 ] && [ "$day" -le 31 ] || die "bad day in $d"
  printf '%s' "$d"
}

# Per-run working area: $WORK_DIR/<date>
run_dir() { printf '%s/%s' "$WORK_DIR" "$1"; }

# Active partner codes, one per line.
active_partners() {
  require_file "$PARTNERS_FILE" "partner list"
  awk -F'|' '!/^#/ && NF >= 4 && $4 == "A" { print $1 }' "$PARTNERS_FILE"
}
# dates.sh — business date helpers (GNU date).

# "20261005" -> "2026-10-05"
date_dash() { printf '%s-%s-%s' "${1:0:4}" "${1:4:2}" "${1:6:2}"; }

# "2026-10-05" or "20261005" -> "20261005"
date_compact() { local d=${1//-/}; printf '%s' "$d"; }

# date_next YYYYMMDD -> the following calendar day
date_next() { date -u -d "$(date_dash "$1") +1 day" +%Y%m%d; }

# date_range FROM TO — every calendar day from FROM to TO inclusive.
# Partners settle seven days a week, so weekends are included.
date_range() {
  local d=$1 end=$2 guard=0
  while [ "$d" -le "$end" ]; do
    printf '%s\n' "$d"
    d=$(date_next "$d")
    guard=$((guard + 1))
    [ "$guard" -le 400 ] || { warn "date range too long: $1..$2"; return 1; }
  done
}

# receipts_day ROWS DATE -> "<count> <net> <have> <want>" for the day.
# The detail rows in the box are those of the parts that arrived, so they are
# totalled as they are. <have> of <want> parts are in the box; a day with
# have 0 (no file at all) is shown as '-' by the caller.
receipts_day() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk -F'\t' -v d="$2" '
    $1 == "P" && $2 == d { seen[$3 + 0] = 1; want = $4 + 0 }
    $1 == "D" && $2 == d { n++; s += $3 }
    END {
      have = 0
      for (p in seen) if (p >= 1 && p <= want) have++
      print n + 0, s + 0, have + 0, want + 0
    }'
}

# receipts_report PARTNER FROM TO
# A partial split day (have < want) shows its arrived rows with "have/want
# 파일"; the partner loads the day only once all parts are in, so these are
# not the loadable totals (see docs/runbook-oncall.md).
